youtube_title: Knox, Indiana: the night a crowd said it saw Halley's Comet sparks (1910)
youtube:
You asked for Knox! In 1910, astronomers had found a poison gas, cyanogen, in the tail of Halley's Comet, and Earth was expected to pass through it. People bought comet pills, and some sealed up their houses. In Knox, folks turned to a local lawyer known for his astronomy, who said he'd explain it all on a street corner. Several hundred people came. He told them about the comet and kept pointing up: "Just look at those sparks." At first only he saw them. Then the whole crowd said they saw glowing sparks too. That's how Alexander Jonas retold it on WKVI radio around 1970, from a story state senator Oliver Cannon told him, and he called it mass hysteria. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Knox #StarkeCounty #Indiana #HalleysComet #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. The Knox story comes from one source: Alexander L. Jonas, "Knox Characters I Have Known" (his WKVI talks, 1969-70, in the Starke County Public Library's local history collection). Other sources: Starke County Historical Society, Past Tidbits #06 and #31; Sam Kean, "The Comet Panic of 1910, Revisited," Science History Institute (2025); Astronomy, "Unlocking the mystery of comets" (2023); The Conversation, "Halley's comet, COVID-19 and the history of miracle anti-comet remedies"; E. E. Barnard, Astrophysical Journal (1914). More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

factcheck: Two blind checks Nov. 16, 2026 (script, text and pictures only; the second on the changes). The Knox crowd rests on one source, Jonas's 'Knox Characters I Have Known' (Chapter Six), made with Scoop's OK. Fixes: 'Earth was about to pass through it' became 'was expected to' (later calculations and Nature, 1910, say the tail probably missed); line 7 now says Jonas retold it 'from a story state senator Oliver Cannon told him' (Jonas came to Knox from 1914; the 'state senator' title rests on Jonas); the comet was taken out of the sealed-window picture (that night its head was between Earth and the Sun); credits name Jonas's WKVI talks and Astronomy's own 2023 article. The typed 'MASS HYSTERIA' was cut off by the end card on the first render, so it now types from 'He called it' with a short pause.
